fallbacks: Horns Rev 16: all runs from mpce_hrfix (corrected direction binning, 970 runs); 1000 runs of the old model dropped
ranking_rule: Within each case a method is ranked by the mean objective of its feasible runs only if at least half of its runs (15 of 30; 5 of 10) are feasible; methods with fewer feasible runs receive the worst ranks, below all qualifying methods, ordered by their number of feasible runs (more = better, ties averaged). This removes the survivorship bias of ranking by the mean feasible objective.

subgroup_vs_phase1.note: exploratory, post hoc split at N >= 10; case-mean Wilcoxon unadjusted; run-level W/T/L from the main-table family (Holm over the 7 comparisons of the focus in each case)

case_mean_imputation.note: a case in which exactly one of the two methods has >= 15 feasible runs enters the case-mean test with a difference larger than every observed one in favour of that method (imputed); cases in which neither has are dropped; counts summed over the comparisons of the main table

holm_families.main_wtl: per case: PSO-VNS vs each of the other 7 methods of the main comparison (Table wtl, tab:friedman68 p_W over the 7 methods)
holm_families.ablation: per case: the planned contrasts of Table ablation (run level); case-mean p_W of Table ablation: Holm over the same contrasts
holm_families.baseline: per case: the hybrid vs each of the other 7 methods of the previous study's pool (Table baseline)
holm_families.split: per case: the 6 run-level comparisons of the split table (PSOBV vs PSOBV25, PSOBV vs PSOBV75, PSOBV vs PSOBV90, PSOBV vs PSOC, PSOBV75 vs PSOC, PSOBV90 vs PSOBV75)
holm_families.hr16: per setting: the focus vs each other method
holm_families.feasinit: per case: feasible vs random initialization, over the methods of the case
holm_families.why_psovns_vs_pso_differs: The main-table tally (Holm over 7 comparisons) and the ablation tally (Holm over the ablation contrasts) use the same per-case raw p-values of PSO-VNS vs PSO but different Holm families, so the adjusted p and hence W/T/L differ; both are descriptive tallies.

baseline.note: 'PSO' denotes the PSO of the respective pool: old = w 0.7, c1 = c2 = 2 (fresh_grid PSO); constriction = Clerc-Kennedy (PSOC). W/T/L from the hybrid's side, Holm over the 7 comparisons of the hybrid within each case.

cost_per_eval.data: 6,030-evaluation runs of the 68 cases (random initialization), ms = Seconds / Calls * 1000, median over runs

cost.note: wall-clock times come from the machine that produced each file; runs from different files may not be directly comparable

ablation.holm_family: per case, over the 15 contrasts (run level); case-mean p_holm over the same 15 contrasts

PSOBV-BVNS.isolates: swarm start vs. best initial point

RSVNS.note: Phase-1 samples = 30 common initial layouts (square) + 2,985 samples (square for RS-VNS, disc for RSD-VNS); counts over both data sets (identical geometry and seeds)

RSDVNS.note: Phase-1 samples = 30 common initial layouts (square) + 2,985 samples (square for RS-VNS, disc for RSD-VNS); counts over both data sets (identical geometry and seeds)

square_vs_disc.note: paired over runs (case, seed, both data sets): rs_none_rsd_some = RS-VNS runs without a feasible Phase-1 sample that disc sampling would rescue (the most the square can explain); rs_none_rsd_none = runs without a feasible sample even when sampling in the disc (spacing / packing density)

equivalence.margin_note: one margin for every case-mean comparison, chosen after the primary analysis (post hoc); min_margin_pp = smallest margin at which the 90 % CI lies inside (-m, m)
equivalence.rule: equivalent iff the 90 % percentile bootstrap CI of the mean case-mean difference lies strictly inside (-m, m) (TOST, alpha 0.05)
equivalence.p_tost: nonparametric bootstrap TOST p (add-one, floor 1/(BOOT_N+1)); p_tost_t = paired-t TOST on the case means, for reference

bayes.test: Bayesian signed-rank test (Benavoli et al. 2017, JMLR 18:77)
bayes.probabilities: share of posterior samples in which each of theta_A, theta_rope, theta_B is the largest

equivalence.case_set: cases in which both methods have >= 15 of 30 feasible runs (as mean_dloss_pp / ci95 of the \NCm macros)
equivalence.sign: d = L(A) - L(B), pp; negative = A (first method) better

spread.note: per case: SD of the wake loss (%) of the feasible runs and loss of the worst feasible run, 30 runs, 6,030 evaluations; wins = cases in which PSO-VNS has the smaller SD / lower worst-run loss (|d| <= 1e-9 = tie); Wilcoxon signed-rank on the per-case values (ties dropped), unadjusted; rb > 0 = PSO-VNS smaller

split.holm_family: per case, over the 6 run-level comparisons PSOBV vs PSOBV25, PSOBV vs PSOBV75, PSOBV vs PSOBV90, PSOBV vs PSOC, PSOBV75 vs PSOC, PSOBV90 vs PSOBV75

hr_validation.note: installed 80-turbine Horns Rev 1 farm, hornsrev_model.py (current binning) vs the PyWake Jensen reference value quoted in hornsrev_site_text.tex (662.5 GWh/yr, 10.96 %)

hr16.holm_family: per setting, PSO-VNS vs each of the other 9 methods

budget.note: HR16 at 120,030 calls uses 10 seeds (qualification: at least 5 feasible runs)

decision.dloss_sign: dL = L(PSOBV) - L(other) in percentage points of the wake loss; negative = PSO-VNS better
decision.wtl_sign: W/T/L from the PSO-VNS side (W = PSO-VNS significantly better)
